source.title: Main battle tank
source.quote: The extreme weight of vehicles of this type 40–70 t (39–69 long tons; 44–77 short tons) also limits their speed.

mass_kg.note: Upper figure of the stated 40-70 t range for main battle tanks; the source gives no mean. Low and high keep the stated range.

size_m.note: Stand-in: the hull length of one modern main battle tank (M1 Abrams, gun not counted), used for a generic tank because the Main battle tank article gives no length. Range is +/-25%.

source.title: Main battle tank
source.quote: However, tracks are not as fast as wheels; the maximum speed of a tank is about 65 km/h (40 mph).

top_speed_mps.note: 65 km/h = 18.06 m/s. Range is the standard +/-10%.

attack_force_n.note: Ramming machine: attack_force_n = RAM_DAMAGE_PER_MOMENTUM x mass_kg x top_speed_mps / DAMAGE_PER_NEWTON (0.005 x 70,000 x 18.06 / 0.05). The engine works out the real hit from mass and speed. Low and high use the low and high mass and speed.

attacks_per_s.note: Ramming machine: RAM_ATTACKS_PER_S, the engine's fixed ramming rate.

endurance_s.note: Vehicle: endurance = range / top_speed_mps = 500,000 m / 18.06 m/s. Range from Main battle tank (https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Main_battle_tank&oldid=1384871486): "with an operational range near 500 km (310 mi)". Driving time at top speed, not measured fighting time. Low and high use the high and low speed.

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level M: operated to win, a machine with a driver.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 4: tank platoons fight in radio contact under drilled doctrine.
